## What this report establishes

The full report reproduces the downstream CellCharter workflow from the fixed
published mouse-spleen trVAE representation. It documents the sample-local
graph, neighborhood aggregation, compiled C++ AutoK search, independently
selected K=10 primary result, separately labelled compiled C++ K=11 sensitivity result, cell-type
enrichment, and condition-specific and differential neighborhood enrichment.
It does not claim that CellCharterR regenerated the trVAE representation.

The expensive analysis is not rerun during package installation. Its rendered
HTML contains the preserved code, parameters, provenance, figures, and
limitations. Open either copy:

- [Installed report](../reports/CellCharterR-mouse-spleen-reproducibility.html)
- [Public report](https://cperalta-viteri.github.io/CellCharterR/docs/CellCharterR-mouse-spleen-reproducibility.html)

## Preserved roles

K=10 is the primary resolution selected by the compiled C++ AutoK stability
analysis. The stability curve retains the other peaks so users can inspect
alternative resolutions. K=11 is a standalone tutorial-matched compiled C++
sensitivity fit; it is neither the AutoK selection nor the published H5AD label
vector. The report keeps these roles separate and validates ordered-spot
identity before combining artifacts.

For a small runnable introduction, return to the
[beginner workflow](https://cperalta-viteri.github.io/CellCharterR/docs/CellCharterR-beginner-workflow.html).
For supported downstream analysis from existing domains, continue to the
[differential-neighborhood tutorial](https://cperalta-viteri.github.io/CellCharterR/docs/CellCharterR-differential-neighborhood-networks.html).

```{r locate-installed-report}
report <- system.file(
  "reports", "CellCharterR-mouse-spleen-reproducibility.html",
  package = "CellCharterR"
)
stopifnot(nzchar(report), file.exists(report))
basename(report)
```
